package.title: Buildable cut pieces and honest cut instructions
package.goal: Every planned cut piece is at least as wide as the user's minimum. Triangle edits are validated like line edits. Degenerate pieces can never produce Infinity values. Non-convex stones never get straight cut lines through their own body.
steps: geometry.ts: add convexHull (monotone chain), minCaliperWidth(poly) (minimum over edge normals of the max-min projection, skipping zero-length edges), and minInteriorAngle(poly).
pieces.ts pieceCuttable: only ever tighten. Keep the 2A/P >= min/2 test, AND require minCaliperWidth(isConvex(p) ? p : convexHull(p)) >= min - 1e-6. Do not add a hard rule on angle or edge length.

edits.ts setCellKind: for DIAG_A/DIAG_B, compute the two pieces with diagA/diagB(r, joint). Return 'diag-empty' when cleanPoly gives fewer than 3 points, and 'too-small' when pieceCuttable fails. For SUB, use subRects(...).every(pieceCuttable) in place of the hand-written min(sw,sh) test. Return early without touching progress when the kind and its parameters are unchanged.

edits.ts: export allowedCellKinds(layout, data, row, col, minPieceMm), a dry run of the same checks. Also export repairDegenerateCells(layout, data): number. It turns DIAG/LINE cells with a degenerate piece into FULL, keeps c1, and clears their progress. Wave 2 calls it on load.

pieces.ts analyzeCut: when cleanPoly has fewer than 3 points or the area is below 1e-6, return finite zeros with invalid:true, fits:false, needsCut:false, yieldPerRaw:1 and empty arrays. Add `invalid?: boolean` to CutInfo.

pieces.ts cutLinesFor: for non-convex pieces, split each edge's extended line into intervals at its polygon intersections. Classify each interval by whether its midpoint is strictly inside the piece. Keep the largest contiguous outside run that contains the edge midpoint. Return a parallel cutKinds: ('through'|'notch')[]. Convex output must stay identical. Prefer the placement with the fewest notch cuts.

StoneDialog: show notch cuts with their own text, e.g. 'Einschnitt i: von (x|y) bis Innenecke (x|y) – nicht durchritzen, ausknabbern/schleifen'. Show a 'cut.invalid' message for invalid pieces. Disable the Dreiecke, 2×2 and 3×3 buttons according to allowedCellKinds, with the reason as tooltip.
CutTemplateSvg: draw notch cuts as dotted orange lines. Add an advisory 'schwierig zu schneiden' badge when the minimum angle is below 25°. This is display only.

types.ts: change DEFAULT_SHAPES.minPieceMm from 1.5 to 2.0. In the ext file, override shapes.minPiece to 'Schmalste Stelle eines Schnittteils (mm)' and add a hint key. StepShapes: compute the sub-stone badge (line 29) with the same pieceCuttable(subRects) check, so the badge matches what compute does.
acceptance: Unit tests: pieceCuttable(1×5 rect, 1.5) is false; (1.5×5, 1.5) is true; the diagonal triangle of a 3 mm tile with 1 mm joint stays rejected at 1.5.
On all four samples with Home.tsx settings and DEFAULT_SHAPES, every piece of a DIAG, LINE or SUB cell has minCaliperWidth >= minPieceMm - 1e-6.

setCellKind DIAG on a 2×2 tile with 3 mm joint returns an error and the cell stays FULL. A 2×2 tile with 1 mm joint at min 1.5 gives 'too-small', the same as LINE at 45°. An 8×8 tile with 1 mm joint is accepted.
Clicking 'Ganzer Stein' on a laid FULL cell keeps its progress bit.
analyzeCut([]) returns only finite numbers and invalid:true.
For L, U and chevron fixtures, no sampled point on a cut segment lies strictly inside the piece. Rect, triangle and hexagon cut lines are identical to the old implementation.
With a 3×8 tile, 1 mm joint, k=2 and min 2, the StepShapes badge says no subdivision and compute produces 0 SUB cells.
package.risk: Effort M-L. The stricter width rule changes automatic cut choices, so expect deliberate golden-hash updates by later mosaic owners. Do not touch freeform validation here; wave 3 handles it.

findings.title: The 'Kleinstes Schnittteil 1.5 mm' setting does not limit the real piece width: 1.0 × 5.0 mm glass strips are planned
findings.problem: pieceCuttable (pieces.ts:155-161) accepts a piece when 2·Area/Perimeter ≥ minPieceMm/2. For a w × 5 mm strip that ratio is 10w/(10+2w), so a 1.0 mm strip passes the default 1.5 mm limit. The UI calls the setting 'Kleinstes Schnittteil' (de.ts:200), while StepShapes.tsx:29 compares the sub-stone edge length directly: the same setting has two different meanings. The plan therefore contains slivers that cannot realistically be nipped from glass or ceramic, which conflicts with 'must be buildable with real tiles' and requirement 18.
findings.evidence: Script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/algo-quality/exp-thin.ts (output .../out/results/exp-thin.txt). Obama, 5 mm stones, 1 mm joint, DEFAULT_SHAPES: 40 pieces with a minimum caliper width < 1.3 mm, e.g. A011, C011, E004, E007, Y017, Z017, each 'rectangle 1.00×5.00 mm', 2A/P = 0.833, pieceCuttable = true. Script .../algo-quality/exp-cuts.ts (.../out/results/exp-cuts.txt): share of cut pieces narrower than 2 mm is 29 % (portrait sample), 21.5 % (astronaut) and 19.7 % (obama); about 30 % of cut pieces have an edge shorter than 1.5 mm. App screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/algo-quality/out/browser-preview-zoom.png shows a 1 mm '01' white strip next to the eye. Prototype with minimum caliper width ≥ 2.0 mm (exp-proto.ts): 0 % of pieces under 2 mm and 4–6 % fewer cut pieces. Perceived ΔE: obama 1.38→1.44, astronaut 1.93→1.97, portrait 0.97→0.75.
findings.proposal: Replace the criterion with exact geometry in one shared function, cutFeasible(poly, minPieceMm). It requires: minimum caliper width ≥ minPieceMm (for convex pieces, rotating calipers over the edge normals); shortest edge ≥ 0.5·minPieceMm; smallest interior angle ≥ 30°. edgeLengths and interiorAngles already exist in geometry.ts. Use it in mosaic.ts (all three split types), edits.ts (manual shape changes), free-form validation and StepShapes. Make the default relative to the tile, e.g. max(2 mm, 0.35·min(tileW, tileH)), and label it 'schmalste Stelle eines Schnittteils'. Optionally show a cutting-difficulty badge on each cut template.
corrected:
1) In src/core/pieces.ts, replace the body of pieceCuttable(poly, minPieceMm) with a minimum-width test. For each edge, project all vertices onto that edge's unit normal. The width is (max − min) of those projections, and the smallest width over all edges is the exact narrowest dimension for a convex polygon. Accept the piece when that width >= minPieceMm − 1e-6. If isConvex(poly) is false (free-form pieces only), compute the same width on the convex hull and also keep the old test 2A/P >= minPieceMm/2. That is still only an approximation, so it may only warn, as validateFreePieces already does. The call sites in mosaic.ts (256, 343, 369) and edits.ts (54, 102) then become consistent automatically. edits.ts:62 and StepShapes.tsx:29 already compare widths directly and match the new meaning.

2) Change DEFAULT_SHAPES.minPieceMm in src/core/types.ts from 1.5 to 2.0, the same as the border minimum DEFAULT_SETTINGS.minCutMm = 2. Keep it user-editable. Existing projects keep their stored value but get the correct width meaning on the next compute.

3) Make the label say what is measured. de.ts:200 → 'Schmalste Stelle eines Schnittteils (mm)', with a hint such as 'Kein geschnittenes Teil wird schmaler als dieser Wert'. Update en.ts and tr.ts the same way.

4) Do NOT add hard limits on interior angle or edge length. A 30° minimum would forbid diagonals on 4×8 mm tiles (26.6°), and a minimum edge length would reject truncated near-triangles. At most, show an advisory 'schwierig zu schneiden' badge on the cut template when the smallest angle is under about 25°. This is display only and never changes the geometry or the dimensions shown.

5) Add a vitest test: compute a sample with DEFAULT_SHAPES and assert that every piece from a non-full cell has a minimum width >= minPieceMm. Also unit-test pieceCuttable directly: a 1×5 mm strip at a 1.5 mm limit must return false, and a 1.5×5 mm strip must return true.

1. **One shared check in pieces.ts**, `cutCheck(poly, minPieceMm): { ok, minWidth, minAngle, reasons }`.
   - `minWidth` is the exact minimum caliper width over all edge directions. All automatic pieces are convex, so this is exact for them.
   - Hard rules for automatic cuts: minWidth ≥ minPieceMm − 1e-9, and minAngle ≥ 20°. The 20° rule only removes the 15° wedges, because cut lines use 15° steps.
   - No shortest-edge rule: in portrait 8×8, all 40 pieces with an edge under 0.75 mm are at least 2.4 mm wide at their narrowest.
   - Keep `pieceCuttable` as a thin wrapper, or replace it at every call: mosaic.ts:256/343/369 and edits.ts:54.
   - Replace the separate subdivision checks with the same function: the min(sw, sh) check in edits.ts:62 and the badge test at StepShapes.tsx:29. The badge then matches what the compute step does; this fixes the 3×8 mm tile case.

2. **Free-form pieces (validateFreePieces).** Thickness = min(caliper width of the convex hull, smallest distance between non-adjacent edges). The second term catches thin necks in concave shapes. Keep it a warning there, as today, and show the measured mm value.

3. **Default and wording.**
   - Change DEFAULT_SHAPES.minPieceMm from 1.5 to 2.0. This is the value the prototype tested.
   - Rename the setting in de/en/tr: "Schmalste Stelle eines Schnittteils" / "Narrowest point of a cut piece".
   - Add a hint: "Größerer Wert = leichter schneidbar, aber weniger feine Konturen."
   - Optionally show a recommended value next to the field, e.g. "Empfehlung für 8-mm-Glas: 2,5 mm", with an "Übernehmen" button. Do not apply a hidden tile-relative formula, and never overwrite a value the user entered.

4. **Existing plans: show, don't recompute.**
   - Do not force a recompute (computeKey stays the same, so progress and manual edits are kept).
   - Add a read-only check over the computed plan: count pieces narrower than the setting.
   - Show a badge "unter Mindestbreite (x,x mm) – schwer schneidbar" in StoneDialog and on that piece's cut template, plus a count in StepPreview with the note "Neu berechnen, um zu ersetzen".
   - Never change existing geometry.

5. **Tests (vitest).**
   - A 1×5 mm rectangle fails at 1.5.
   - 2×2 subdivision of a 5 mm tile with a 1 mm joint (2.0×2.0 mm pieces) passes at 2.0.
   - A 15° triangle fails.
   - On all four samples at default settings, no cut piece is narrower than minPieceMm.
   - The 3×8 mm tile case: no subdivision when the badge says none will happen.
   - Piece-count and geometry tests still pass unchanged.

Effort S–M (concave free-form check and badges included). Impact 4.

findings.title: Minimum piece size is only half enforced: auto and manual cuts create strips narrower than minPieceMm
findings.problem: pieceCuttable accepts a piece when 2*area/perimeter >= minPieceMm/2. For a w x h strip that is w*h/(w+h) >= min/2, so long strips pass at roughly half the minimum width (a 1.0 x 8 mm strip passes a 1.5 mm minimum). The UI presents the setting as 'kleinstes zulässiges Schnittteil'. The auto computation and the manual LINE edit therefore produce slivers below the user's limit. setCellKind(SUB) uses a different, strict rule (min(sw, sh) < minPiece), so the two paths are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: src/core/pieces.ts:154-161; used at src/core/mosaic.ts:256,343,369 and src/core/edits.ts:54,102; strict variant at edits.ts:62. Repro /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-core/r7_minpiece.ts output: 'pieceCuttable(1.0 x 8 strip, min 1.5) = true'; 'manual LINE 0°, offset 2.5 mm, minPiece 1.5: result=accepted; piece widths=6.00 / 1.00'. Auto compute (300x400 mm, 8 mm tile, 1 mm joint, detail 0.8): 'portrait minPiece=1.5: 14 of 372 cut pieces are narrower than minPiece (narrowest 1.00 mm)', 'animal ... 39 of 494', 'city ... 72 of 458'; with minPiece=2 the narrowest piece is 1.50 mm.
findings.proposal: Replace the criterion with the minimum caliper width. For convex pieces: minWidth(poly) = min over edges e of (max over vertices v of the distance from v to line(e)), as in r7_minpiece.ts. Require minWidth >= minPieceMm - 1e-9. Use the same function in mosaic.ts (tryTwo, LINE scan, SUB), edits.ts (LINE, SUB, freeform warning) and in the StepShapes warning, so auto and manual edits follow one rule. Add a pipeline test asserting minWidth >= minPieceMm for every non-FULL piece.
corrected:
Tighten the rule in `pieceCuttable` (`src/core/pieces.ts`) instead of replacing it.

1. Add `minCaliperWidth(poly)`. Run it on `convexHull(poly)`: for each edge, take the largest distance from any vertex to that edge's line; the result is the smallest of those values.
2. Accept a piece only if BOTH hold:
   - the existing check, `2*A/P >= min/2 - 1e-9`
   - `minCaliperWidth(poly) >= min - 1e-9`

   This rejects strips narrower than the minimum. It never accepts anything rejected today, so triangles are not loosened.
3. For non-convex polygons (freeform pieces), caliper width is not a thickness measure. Additionally require `2*A/P >= min` (the full minimum, not half), and say in the "free.thin" warning text that the thickness check for freeform pieces is approximate. The freeform check only produces a warning, so nothing is blocked.
4. Make `setCellKind` SUB (`edits.ts:62`) and the StepShapes warning use the same function, or provably the same rule, so automatic and manual edits behave the same.
5. Add a vitest that runs `computeMosaic` on the four samples with default shapes and checks that every non-FULL piece has `minCaliperWidth >= minPieceMm - 1e-6`.
6. Add a unit test that `setCellKind(LINE, angle 0, offset 2.5)` on an 8 mm tile with a 1 mm joint and min 1.5 returns `'too-small'`.

Effort: S. Impact: 3.

Tighten the rule only. Do not replace the existing test, and use one rule everywhere.

1) In src/core/pieces.ts, add `minCaliperWidth(poly)` for convex polygons. It works on cleanPoly(poly), skips zero-length edges, and returns the minimum over edges e of the maximum over vertices v of |cross(e, v-e0)|/|e|. Change pieceCuttable to: `if (2A/P < min/2 - 1e-9) return false; return minCaliperWidth(isConvex(p) ? p : convexHull(p)) >= min - 1e-9;`. Rectangles then need their shorter side >= min, the same as the SUB rule. Triangles keep today's inscribed-circle rule, so no piece that is rejected today becomes accepted. LINE pentagons and quadrilaterals have to pass both tests.

2) Use the one function everywhere. mosaic.ts:256/343/369 already call it. In edits.ts:62, replace the hand-written `Math.min(sw, sh) < minPieceMm` with `subRects(r, k, g).every(p => pieceCuttable(p, min))`. Have StepShapes.tsx:29 call the same helper on a sample cell. Then the 'wird nicht unterteilt' badge, auto SUB (currently 7 SUB cells despite the badge in the 4x8 / joint 1 / min 2 case) and manual SUB all agree.

3) FREE pieces (edits.ts:102, a warning only). For concave pieces the hull width is only an upper bound. Keep the 2A/P test as well, and add the note '(bei nicht-konvexen Teilen nur näherungsweise geprüft)' to 'free.thin' in de/en/tr. Do not claim an exact check.

4) Old projects keep their stored 1 mm strips. On the plan/material step, add a count computed from the stored geometry: 'N Schnittteile sind schmaler als X mm – neu berechnen'. List the stone IDs, and do not alter the data silently.

5) Add a hint to 'shapes.minPiece' in all 3 languages: 'schmalste Stelle jedes Schnittteils'.

6) Tests:
- pipeline: for all 4 samples with min 1.5 and 2, every non-FULL, non-FREE piece has minCaliperWidth >= min - 1e-6.
- unit: pieceCuttable(1x8 rect, 1.5) is false, and the diagonal triangle for tile 3 / joint 1 / min 1.5 stays rejected.
- edits: LINE at 0°, offset 2.5 mm, on an 8 mm tile with 1 mm joint and min 1.5 returns 'too-small'; SUB on a 4x8 tile with min 2 returns 'too-small', the same as auto.

findings.title: 'Kleinstes Schnittteil' is not enforced as a width, so the app plans 1 mm glass slivers that cannot be cut
findings.problem: Requirement 1 says the plan must be buildable with real tiles. Automatic cuts are validated with 2·Area/Perimeter ≥ min/2. For a 10 mm long strip that accepts widths down to 0.81 mm, although the UI labels the setting (default 1.5 mm) as the smallest cut piece. The manual 2×2 check uses the real width (edits.ts:62), so the two checks disagree. Material thickness (default 4 mm) is ignored. A 1 × 10 mm strip from a 4 mm thick glass tile cannot be cut with nippers. The cut dimensions are correct, but the plan cannot be built.
findings.evidence: src/core/pieces.ts:155-161 (pieceCuttable formula). This check is used in src/core/mosaic.ts:256, :343 and :369. Measurement /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/spec-gaps/core2.ts (output in core2.out), with exact minimum caliper width per piece. City sample (10 mm tiles, 2 mm joint): '301 pieces min width <=1.0mm', for example '1.00x10.00 minW=1.00'. Portrait 5 mm: 16 pieces ≤1.0 mm and 192 pieces <2 mm. Landscape: 30 pieces <1.5 mm (8.00x1.25). core1.out lists 'rectangle 1x10:257' for the city sample. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/spec-gaps/shots/b2-eyes.png shows hairline 02/03 strips on the eye cells.
findings.proposal: Replace pieceCuttable with exact geometric tests. (a) Minimum caliper width: the minimum over all edge normals of max−min projection. This is exact because every automatic piece is convex. Require it to be ≥ minPieceMm. (b) Minimum interior angle ≥ a configurable value, e.g. 25°, to reject needle triangles. (c) In the LINE search (mosaic.ts ~320-350), clamp the offset range analytically so that both halves keep that width, which avoids evaluating useless candidates. (d) Default minPieceMm by surface, e.g. 3 mm for glass, and relabel it 'Mindestbreite eines Schnittteils'. Warn when it is below the thickness of the assigned material. (e) Add a stats counter 'Teile unter Mindestbreite' (must be 0) and a vitest assertion over the four samples that every automatic piece has minWidth ≥ the setting.
corrected:
1. **Fix the check in src/core/pieces.ts.** Add `minCaliperWidth(poly)`: the minimum over edge normals of (max − min projection). Rewrite `pieceCuttable(poly, min)` to return `minCaliperWidth(poly) >= min - 1e-6`. This is exact for automatic pieces, which are all convex: diagonal triangles, half-plane clips of a rectangle, and sub-rectangles. The call sites in mosaic.ts:256/343/369 and edits.ts:54 then enforce a real width with no other change. Today's 1.0 mm strips become the next valid offset (≥1.5 mm) or stay full stones.

2. **Free pieces.** In `validateFreePieces` (edits.ts:102), warn if the convex-hull width is below the minimum OR if the existing 2A/P heuristic fails. Keep it a warning, because hull width cannot see thin parts of non-convex pieces.

3. **Optional angle check.** Add a minimum interior angle (for example 20°) to reject needle tips. Only add it with a vitest showing it does not block the diagonal of every custom tile size the user listed (3×5, 4×8, 6×10, 8×12).

4. **Do not raise the default to 3 mm.**
   - Keep 1.5 mm, or raise it at most to 2 mm.
   - Relabel the field in de/en/tr as "Mindestbreite eines Schnittteils" and add a hint explaining what it means.
   - In StepShapes, extend the existing subTooSmall badge with a computed note listing which cut types are impossible at the current tile, joint and minimum. For example, with 5 mm tiles, a 1 mm joint and a 3 mm minimum, only diagonals remain.
   - Optionally show an advisory when the minimum is below the thickness of the assigned material (Material.thicknessMm). Do not change cuts automatically.

5. **Count and test.**
   - Add a counter "Teile unter Mindestbreite" (must be 0) to stats.ts.
   - Add a vitest in tests/pipeline.test.ts that computes the four samples with the Home.tsx settings and asserts every automatic piece satisfies `minCaliperWidth >= shapes.minPieceMm`.
   - Add unit tests: pieceCuttable(1×10, 1.5) === false and pieceCuttable(1.5×10, 1.5) === true.

Effort: S for steps 1, 2 and 5; M if the thickness advisory is included.

1. src/core/pieces.ts: add `minWidthConvex(poly)`. For each edge, project all vertices onto the edge normal and take max−min; the smallest value is the width, skipping zero-length edges. Change `pieceCuttable(poly, min)` to `area > 0 && minWidthConvex(poly) >= min − 1e-6` for convex polygons. Every automatic piece is convex: diagonal triangles, line-cut pieces from clipHalfPlane, sub rectangles and edge rectangles. For those the test is exact. Keep the call sites mosaic.ts:256/343/369 and edits.ts:54 unchanged, and let edits.ts:62 call the same function so all checks share one rule.

2. Freeform pieces (edits.ts:102, non-convex allowed): use a local-thickness test instead of the edge-normal width. Rasterize the piece at 0.05 mm (at most 240×240 px per cell), apply a morphological opening with a disc of diameter min, and warn if more than about 0.5% of the area is lost. Keep this as a warning, not an error, and word it as an approximate check ('ca. ±0,05 mm').

3. Settings and texts: keep the value user-editable. Raise DEFAULT_SHAPES.minPieceMm from 1.5 to 2.0. This was measured on the four samples: detail is kept, no 1 mm strips remain, and a 3 mm default would wipe out portrait detail. Relabel 'shapes.minPiece' in de/en/tr as 'Mindestbreite eines Schnittteils' / 'Minimum width of a cut piece' / 'Kesim parçasının en küçük genişliği'. Add a hint: 'schmalste Stelle eines geschnittenen Teils (ohne Fuge). Erfahrungswert: bei 4 mm dickem Glas sind Teile unter ca. 2–3 mm schwer zu knipsen.' Present it as a recommendation, not a rule. No hard dependence on material thickness, because 4 mm is the default for every material and a warning tied to it would fire almost always.

4. Angle test: no hard reject. With the 2 mm default no sample piece has an angle under 20°; at 1.5 mm landscape has 23 (compare outputs). At most, add an info counter 'Teile mit Spitzwinkel < 20°' in stats.

5. src/core/stats.ts: add a `minPieceMm` option and a `thinPieces` counter for pieces with width < setting. Automatic pieces must be 0; freeform warnings are counted separately. Show it in StepPlan / the material summary. Projects saved with the old check keep their old pieces, so for them show a badge 'X Teile schmaler als Mindestbreite – Neuberechnung empfohlen'.

6. Tests:
   - tests/pipeline.test.ts: for all four samples with the Home.tsx settings, assert that every piece of a diagonal, line or sub cell has minWidthConvex ≥ shapes.minPieceMm − 1e-6.
   - tests/core.test.ts: for lineSplit on a 10 mm cell with a 2 mm joint at d = −3, assert pieceCuttable(·, 1.5) === false; assert that setCellKind line and sub on the same cell reject or accept consistently; assert that the 0.8 mm L-shaped freeform piece produces a 'thin' warning.

7. Drop the analytic offset clamping in the line search (perf only, risk of off-by-one bugs).

findings.title: Cut lines for non-convex freeform stones cut straight through the stone
findings.problem: analyzeCut/cutLinesFor extends every edge that is not on the raw tile's border into a straight line across the whole raw tile. That is only valid for convex pieces. For a non-convex freeform piece (L shape, notch), StoneDialog and the PDF list 'Schnitt 1: von ... nach ...' lines that run through the piece's interior. Following them destroys the stone. The only hint is 'Nicht konvex: nur mit Nachschleifen/Feinzange exakt herstellbar', next to wrong numeric cut instructions. This violates requirement 18 (never show wrong cut dimensions).
findings.evidence: src/core/pieces.ts:200-218 (lineThroughRect on every edge), consumed by src/ui/project/StoneDialog.tsx:26 and src/core/pdf.ts:766,789. Repro /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-core/r3_free_nonconvex.ts (10x10 cell, L piece with a 6x6 notch, accepted by setFreePieces): output 'Schnitt 1: (0|4) -> (10|4)', 'Schnitt 2: (4|0) -> (4|10)'; geometric checker: 'line (0.00,4.00)-(10.00,4.00) crosses piece interior; convex=false' and the same for the second line. The correct cuts would stop at the reflex vertex (4|4).
findings.proposal: In cutLinesFor, emit segments instead of full lines when !isConvex(polyInRaw). For each edge a->b, cast a ray from b forward and from a backward. Stop each ray at the first hit on the raw border or on another edge of the piece (ray/segment intersection), and output [hitBack, hitFwd]. Segments that end at a reflex vertex become notch cuts ('Einschnitt bis (x|y)'). If that is out of scope, the minimal fix for requirement 18 is: for non-convex pieces return cutLines = [], label the template 'nur Kontur (1:1) – keine durchgehenden Schnittlinien', and do not print 'Schnitt i' lines in StoneDialog or pdf.ts. Add a property test that no cut line passes through a piece's interior (checkCut in the scratch lib.ts does this).
corrected:
1) src/core/geometry.ts: add `convexHull(poly: Pt[]): Pt[]` (monotone chain). Add `extendRay(p, dir, poly, W, H)`, which returns the first point where the ray from p hits the raw border or a piece edge, for t > eps. If a test point at p + dir*eps lies inside the piece (`pointInPolygon`), it returns p, so the ray length is 0.

2) src/core/pieces.ts `analyzeCut`: if `isConvex(placed.poly)`, keep the current behaviour. Otherwise set:
   (a) `cutLines` = the `cutLinesFor` result of `convexHull(placed.poly)`. These are straight cuts through the whole raw tile and can be scored and snapped. They never enter the piece, because the hull contains it.
   (b) A new field `notches: Pt[][]` = the pockets between hull and piece. Each pocket is the polygon from one hull edge back along the piece's own vertices. Show each pocket with its edge lengths and its reflex vertex as "Ausklinkung k: Bereich … mit Zange/Schleifer entfernen, Innenecke bei (x|y)". Do NOT show it as a straight cut. Optionally, also emit the notch edges as partial cuts from the hull edge to the reflex vertex, using `extendRay`, and label them "Einschnitt bis (x|y) – nicht brechbar".
   Fallback if (b) is out of scope: for non-convex pieces return `cutLines = []`, and label the template "nur Kontur 1:1 – keine durchgehenden Schnittlinien". Do this in StoneDialog `cutInstruction`, CutTemplateSvg, and pdf.ts:766/789 via new i18n keys in de/en/tr.

3) Change the i18n `cut.nonConvex` / `pdf.nonConvex` text so it refers to the notch instructions instead of generic grinding advice.

4) tests/core.test.ts: add a property test. For random simple polygons inside a cell, including the L, V-notch and arrow from verify-correctness-core-2/v1.ts, no `cutLines` segment may contain a point whose two sides, offset by ±0.05 mm, are both inside the piece. Also assert that the hull plus the notches rebuild the piece's area exactly.

1) src/core/pieces.ts, cutLinesFor: for each edge a-b, keep full = lineThroughRect(a,b,W,H) as today, then trim it as follows. Do not cast rays to the 'next non-adjacent edge'.
   - Parameterise the line as P(t), t in [0,1].
   - Collect every t where the line meets an edge of the polygon (for collinear edges, use both endpoints), plus 0 and 1. Sort them and remove duplicates.
   - For each interval, test whether its midpoint lies strictly inside the polygon (pointInPolygon and not on the boundary).
   - Output the largest run of contiguous 'not strictly inside' intervals that contains the edge midpoint (a+b)/2.
   - Also return through = (both endpoints lie on the raw-tile border). Store this in CutInfo as a new parallel field cutKinds: ('through'|'notch')[]. A new field keeps the existing consumers of cutLines compiling.
   - For convex pieces this gives the same result as today.
   - Prefer the placement candidate with the fewest notch cuts first, then the fewest cuts overall.

2) StoneDialog.tsx:26, pdf.ts:766/789 and CutTemplateSvg.tsx:19:
   - Through cuts keep the 'Schnitt i: von … nach … mm' wording.
   - Notch cuts get a separate string, e.g. de: 'Einschnitt {i}: von (x|y) bis Innenecke (x|y) mm – nicht durchritzen, mit Mosaikzange ausknabbern bzw. schleifen'. Add en and tr versions too.
   - Draw notch cuts in a different style, e.g. dotted orange.
   - Replace the vague 'nicht konvex – nachschleifen' with this concrete text.

3) If time is short, the minimal fix that still satisfies requirement 18 is:
   - When !convex, return cutLines = [].
   - Show 'Nur Kontur 1:1 – Schnittlinien für nicht-konvexe Steine nicht berechnet', in the UI and in the PDF.
   - Never print through-lines for such stones.

4) Tests in tests/core.test.ts:
   - Add fixtures L, U and chevron, and check that no point sampled on any cut segment lies strictly inside polyInRaw.
   - Check that every non-border edge of the piece is covered by some cut segment, so the stone is completely separated.
   - Check that the convex outputs (rect, triangle, hexagon) are unchanged compared to the current implementation.

findings.title: Manual triangle edit (DIAG) is not validated: empty or too-small stones, Infinity in stats and CSV
findings.problem: setCellKind validates LINE (empty piece -> 'line-outside', pieceCuttable -> 'too-small') and SUB (too-small), but DIAG_A/DIAG_B are accepted unconditionally. On narrow edge cells this creates triangles below the minimum size. When the joint is wider than about twice the cell's narrow side, clipping returns empty polygons that are still counted as 2 stones. analyzeCut on an empty polygon reports fits=true, needsCut=true, w/h=-Infinity, and the CSV prints Infinity coordinates.
findings.evidence: src/core/edits.ts:44-46 vs :47-56 (LINE) and :58-66 (SUB); src/core/pieces.ts:238-291 (no guard for poly.length < 3). Repro /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-core/r1_diag_no_validation.out. A: 8 mm tile, 1 mm joint, cut-end, minCut 2, 2 mm edge column: 'SUB k=2 -> too-small', 'DIAG_A -> null', triangles 1.48 x 5.94 mm with cuttable(1.5)=false. B: joint 3, minCut 1, 1 mm edge column: 'DIAG_B -> null', 'pieces [ 0, 0 ]', analyzeCut {shape:'custom', w:null(-Inf), fits:true, needsCut:true}, stats perSize key 'custom|-Infinity|-Infinity', CSV row 'A010-1;A1;1;10;1;Infinity;Infinity;-Infinity;-Infinity;0,00;...;custom;ja;...'. Property test t2_pieces.out: 106 empty pieces and 4,360 sub-minimum triangles accepted out of 12,435 random edits.
findings.proposal: In setCellKind, for DIAG_A/DIAG_B compute [p, q] = (kind === DIAG_A ? diagA : diagB)(r, layout.joint). Return 'line-outside' if p or q has fewer than 3 points, and 'too-small' if either fails the size criterion (the same function as the minPiece finding). Expose a pure canSetCellKind() so StoneDialog can disable the 'Dreiecke' buttons on such cells. Guard analyzeCut: when cleanPoly(poly).length < 3 or area < 1e-9, return fits=false with a new `invalid` flag; computeStats and buildCsv should skip such pieces and report them instead of printing Infinity.
corrected:
1. src/core/edits.ts setCellKind: replace the DIAG_A/DIAG_B `break` with:
   `const [p, q] = (ch.kind === CellKind.DIAG_A ? diagA : diagB)(r, layout.joint); if (cleanPoly(p).length < 3 || cleanPoly(q).length < 3) return 'line-outside'; if (!pieceCuttable(p, minPieceMm) || !pieceCuttable(q, minPieceMm)) return 'too-small';`
   Import diagA/diagB from ./pieces. Add a new message key 'edit.err.diag-empty' in de/en/tr ('Die Fuge ist breiter als der Stein – Dreiecksteilung nicht möglich'), because the existing 'line-outside' text talks about a cut line.
2. Export a pure `allowedCellKinds(layout, data, row, col, minPieceMm)` (or `canSetCellKind`) that dry-runs the same checks. In StoneDialog.tsx:257-271, set `disabled` plus a title tooltip on the Dreiecke/2x2/3x3 buttons when not allowed, so the user does not first click and then get an error.
3. Defensive handling for projects already saved with such cells, in src/core/pieces.ts analyzeCut: when `cleanPoly(polyAbs).length < 3 || area < 1e-6`, return early with `invalid: true`, w=h=area=0, fits=false, needsCut=false, yieldPerRaw=0, empty polyInRaw/cutLines/edges/angles (add `invalid?: boolean` to CutInfo).
   - cutInstruction (StoneDialog.tsx:13) shows a dedicated 'cut.invalid' message instead of the notFit text.
   - computeStats (stats.ts:~180) counts these pieces in a new `invalidPieces` counter and skips adding them to pieces, material (rawExact) and perSize; the UI and PDF material page show a warning when invalidPieces > 0.
   - buildCsv writes empty fields instead of Infinity for them.
   Do NOT filter them out of cellPieces, because piece indices drive the stone IDs (A010-1/-2) and the progress bitmask.
   Optionally, on project load, convert invalid DIAG cells back to FULL and keep c1 as the cell color.
4. Tests (tests/edits.test.ts):
   - DIAG on a 2x2 tile with 3 mm joint returns an error, and the cell stays FULL.
   - DIAG on a 2x2 tile with 1 mm joint and minimum piece 1.5 returns 'too-small', the same as LINE at 45°.
   - DIAG on an 8x8 tile with 1 mm joint is accepted.

1) src/core/edits.ts, setCellKind, case DIAG_A/DIAG_B:
   const [p, q] = (ch.kind === CellKind.DIAG_A ? diagA : diagB)(r, layout.joint);
   if (p.length < 3 || q.length < 3 || !pieceCuttable(p, minPieceMm) || !pieceCuttable(q, minPieceMm)) return 'too-small';
   This is the same criterion as mosaic.ts:256, so automatic and manual results stay consistent. Optionally add an error key 'diag-joint-too-wide' to de/en/tr that names the minimum piece size and the joint width.

2) Export a pure canSetCellKind(layout, data, row, col, ch, minPieceMm): string | null. It runs the same checks without changing anything; setCellKind calls it first. In StoneDialog.tsx:255-270, disable the Dreiecke / 2x2 / 3x3 buttons when it returns an error, and show the translated reason as a tooltip and in a small hint line. Keep the existing error message as a fallback.

3) Make analyzeCut defensive (pieces.ts): if cleanPoly(poly).length < 3 or area < 1e-6, return w=h=area=0 (finite), fits=false, needsCut=false, yieldPerRaw=0, cutLines=[], and a new flag invalid=true.

   - csv.ts: print empty dimension fields plus 'ungueltig' instead of Infinity.
   - Step Plan/Preview and the PDF material page: show a red badge "N ungueltige Teile – Zelle zuruecksetzen" that links to those cells.

4) Repair on load: in useProject's load path, after unpackMosaic, scan DIAG/LINE cells whose cellPieces contain a polygon with fewer than 3 points or area below 1e-6. Set them to FULL with the colour of the first piece and clear their progress bit, then show a one-time notice with the number of repaired cells. Do not repair cells that are merely below the minimum size; flag them only, because lowering the minimum is the user's choice.

5) Tests in tests/core.test.ts:
   - setCellKind DIAG on a 2x2 mm tile with 3 mm joint returns 'too-small'.
   - DIAG on 3x3 mm with 2 mm joint and minPiece 1.5 returns 'too-small'.
   - DIAG on 8x8 mm with 1 mm joint is accepted.
   - Property test: for random layouts and edits, every accepted setCellKind leaves cellPieces with polygons of at least 3 points that pass pieceCuttable, and computeStats has no non-finite w/h. Also check stats.pieces == the sum of cellPieceCount.

Impact 3, effort S.

findings.title: Stone editing happens in a modal that hides the mosaic, has no 'lighter/darker' action and no undo
findings.problem: Requirement 13's example is 'make this stone a lighter blue'. Today the user picks from 32 tiny swatches sorted by ΔE, inside a modal whose backdrop covers the mosaic, so they cannot judge the change in context. A wrong click cannot be undone; they have to remember the old colour code.
findings.evidence: shots/j2-04-stone-dialog.png and j2-06-stone-triangle.png: the 980 px modal covers the canvas and the colour grid shows only 2-digit codes. Code: src/ui/project/StoneDialog.tsx:96 (`<Modal … wide>`), :238-253 (colour grid, no lighter/darker), setPieceColor applied immediately. README 'Rückgängig (Undo) | nicht vorhanden'.
findings.proposal: 1) Turn StoneDialog into a non-modal inspector that replaces the legend <aside> in StepPreview/StepPlan while a stone is selected. The canvas stays visible and the selected stone keeps its highlight. Esc deselects. 2) Add 'Heller' and 'Dunkler' buttons: nearest palette entry with ΔL* > +3 or < −3 and minimal Δa*b*, with the target swatch shown on hover. 3) Add an undo/redo stack in useProject that records {idx, piece, before:{color, kind, free}, after} for setPieceColor, setCellKind and setFreePieces, with Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z and toolbar buttons. Persist the last N entries with the mosaic.
corrected:
1) Undo/redo (most important). In useProject.ts keep an in-memory stack of up to about 200 entries, for this session only. Each entry is `{ idx, before: CellSnapshot, after: CellSnapshot }`, where CellSnapshot = `{ kind, c1, c2, sub?: Uint16Array copy, line?: Float32Array copy, free?: FreePiece[] deep copy, progress }`. Add `snapshotCell(data, idx)` and `restoreCell(data, idx, snap)` to src/core/edits.ts and cover them with a vitest round-trip test for every CellKind. Wrap setPieceColor, setCellKind and setFreePieces: take a snapshot before and after each edit. Wrap bulk replaceColor and removePaletteColor as one entry holding the changed indices (or a full copy of c1/c2/sub/free/palette). Add Undo and Redo buttons to the Preview and Plan toolbars and to the inspector, plus Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y. Ignore these shortcuts while focus is in an input. After each undo or redo, call touchMosaic so the stats and the auto-save update. Clear the stack when the mosaic is recomputed. In README.md, change the "Rückgängig" row to "vorhanden (pro Sitzung)".

2) Fix the progress reset. In setCellKind, or in the StoneDialog setKind handler, return early without changes when the requested kind and parameters equal the current ones. Today, clicking the active "Ganzer Stein" button clears the stone's laid mark (edits.ts:76).

3) Lighter/darker. Add "Heller" and "Dunkler" buttons next to the colour picker. Each one picks the palette entry with ΔL* ≥ +3 (or ≤ −3) that has the smallest Δa*b* (ties broken by ΔE2000). Use only existing palette colours, so no colour is ever invented. Disable the button with a tooltip ("keine hellere Palettenfarbe – Farbe in Schritt 5 hinzufügen") when no such entry exists. Show the target code and hex in the button. Anchor the similarity order to the colour the stone had when the inspector opened, so the swatches do not jump after a click. Show the name and ΔE under the selected swatch, not only in the tooltip.

4) Keep the mosaic visible. On screens 980 px and wider, render StoneDialog's content as a non-modal inspector in place of the legend <aside> in StepPreview and StepPlan. It should be a single column, `position: sticky; max-height: calc(100vh - 80px); overflow: auto`, and have no backdrop. The canvas stays interactive, and the selected stone keeps its highlight through Viewer's `highlight` prop. Esc or the close button deselects. On narrow screens, keep the current modal or use a bottom sheet. The nested FreeformEditor can stay a modal.

Ship this in three independent parts, in this order: undo first (most value, least risk), then the docked panel, then lighter/darker.

A) Undo/redo, session-only (do not persist it).
- In src/core/edits.ts add `snapshotCell(data, idx)`. It returns `{kind, c1, c2, sub: copy of Uint16Array | undefined, line: copy of Float32Array | undefined, free: deep copy | undefined, progress}`.
- Add `restoreCell(data, idx, snap)`. It writes every one of those fields back and deletes map entries that are undefined in the snapshot.
- Add `cellEquals(a, b)`.
- In useProject.ts keep `undoStack` and `redoStack` in a ref, capped at 200 entries. Each entry is `{idx, before, after}`.
- Add `api.editCell(idx, mutateFn)`. It snapshots the cell, runs the existing setPieceColor/setCellKind/setFreePieces call, snapshots again, pushes the entry only if something changed, clears redo, then calls `touchMosaic()`, plus `touchProgress()` if progress changed.
- On undo, apply the entry only if the current cell equals `entry.after`. Otherwise drop the entry and show the toast "Änderung kann nicht rückgängig gemacht werden (Stein wurde inzwischen verändert)". This means undo never overwrites later "verlegt" marks.
- Clear both stacks in `compute()` and whenever `setPalette` changes the palette length or order (removePaletteColor remaps indices).
- Route StoneDialog's setPieceColor, setKind and FreeformEditor onSave through `api.editCell`.
- Add Rückgängig/Wiederholen buttons with disabled state and a counter to the toolbars of StepPreview and StepPlan. Add Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z/Ctrl+Y, ignored while focus is in an input.
- Add a vitest test: SUB [3,5,7,9] with progress 101, then FULL, then undo, must restore exactly [3,5,7,9] and 101. Total stats must equal the pre-edit stats.
- Update README.md:152.
- Lay-mode progress toggles are optional. If they are included, they use the same snapshot mechanism.

B) Non-modal inspector at ≥980px.
- Give StoneDialog a `variant: 'panel' | 'modal'` prop. On wide screens render it without Modal, in place of the `<aside className="side">` content of StepPreview and StepPlan. Put a close/back button at the top that returns to the legend or the sections tab. Stack the content in one column (the aside is 340px wide, styles.css:672).
- Keep the canvas interactive. Clicking another stone navigates the panel, Esc deselects, and `highlight={pick}` stays visible.
- Below 980px keep the current Modal, or a bottom sheet, because `.viewer-layout` collapses to one column there.

C) Heller/Dunkler buttons that only offer a real palette colour of the same hue.
- In the colour section show "Heller" and "Dunkler".
- A candidate is a palette colour q where ΔL* is ≥ +3 (or ≤ −3), and the hue/chroma stays close: Δa*b* ≤ 10 and ΔH*ab ≤ 8.
- Among the candidates, pick the smallest |ΔL*| (the next step, not the extreme).
- Show the target swatch, code, name and ΔE on the button. If there is no candidate, disable the button with the hint "Kein hellerer Farbton dieser Farbe in der Palette – im Schritt Farben ergänzen".
- Never create a colour automatically. In materials mode a new colour must come from the material DB (requirement 18).
- Also mark each swatch in the grid with a small ▲/▼ for lighter/darker than the current colour, so touch users get the information that today only exists in the hover title.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.

otherPackagesInThisWave.title: Reliable saving, atomic compute commit and mosaic integrity
4x faster analysis loop, stable custom palettes, safe palette replacement
Correct raw-tile, pack, stock and cost totals
No ghost clicks, no accidental laying taps, correct German number input
Robust material CSV import/export for German Excel
